title: Enhancing Diffraction in SEM: Using Hybrid-Pixel Detectors with Low Energy Sensitivity
content: Among the diffraction techniques used in SEM, EBSD and 4D Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (4D STEM) are the most widely used. EBSD is a well-established technique, while 4D STEM is still emerging. It is an advanced technique that involves scanning an electron beam across a 2D array on a sample while a detector beneath the sample records a 2D pattern for each point the electron beam visits, creating a 4D dataset. This technique is widely used in Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) for a range of applications, such as virtual imaging, orientation analysis, strain mapping, and differential phase contrast.
